report:
PASS for the entire supplied new mathematical body, relative to the six complete caller grants and their clarifications. This corrected report replaces the malformed preceding outputs. The exact proved sector is smooth geometrically integral projective genus-zero curves over complete characteristic-zero real-valued non-Archimedean fields with residue characteristic zero, actual ample rational bundles, raw mass deg L, unrestricted target support, and uniqueness for every actual finite-energy solution at every analytic point. The unrestricted original P16.4 remains open.

All grant applications match. O constructs the genuine operator before target selection, and C applies in the same retained domain. D supplies actual invariant metric descent, extended energy equality, orbit fibers, unique invariant Radon lifts, and continuous-test dual equality. Its equation implication is used only after establishing its antecedents. N is applied after both norming-reference hypotheses are proved. Q is applied after actual polarized algebraic identification with P1. T handles trivial valuations. Historical labels, operational declarations, and the source ledger are data.

The algebraic splitting argument is sound. A finite affine cover has affine intersections by separatedness; quasi-coherent acyclicity makes its Čech complex compute cohomology. Scalar extension tensors every term, and flatness preserves cohomology, so H1(O)=0 persists. A nonconstant global function over an algebraic closure would have closed nonconstant image in P1 while avoiding infinity, contradicting properness. Base change gives H0(X_F,O)=F.

A geometric point descends to finite E0/K and gives a rational degree-one Cartier divisor P. The O(P) sequence gives two sections surjecting onto its fiber; one generates away from P and the other at P. Their ratio f has exactly one simple pole. Successive skyscraper quotients give H1(O(nP))=0 and h0(O(nP))=n+1. Distinct pole orders make 1,f,…,f^n a basis and prove f transcendental. At every closed pole R≠P of a rational q, the minimal polynomial of f(R) evaluated at f is nonzero with positive vanishing order. Sufficient powers cancel all such poles, introducing no others away from P. Thus h(f)q lies in some H0(O(nP)), proving E0(X)=E0(f). No simple-zero assumption is used; characteristic zero excludes inseparable algebraic residue extensions, and these residue fields are distinct from the valued-field residue field.

The rational inverse extends through each DVR by properness. In this projective setting, scaling homogeneous coordinates to integral coordinates with one unit verifies the valuative extension directly. Finitely many affine coordinates and relations extend to a neighborhood after clearing denominators. Separatedness glues the maps; both compositions equal the identity generically and therefore everywhere on reduced integral curves. A finite Galois closure preserves the isomorphism. No genus-zero classification or hidden finite-map theorem is imported.

The bundle identification is actual. Generic trivializations give divisors; div(p)=[R]−deg(p)[∞] for irreducible affine p. Polynomial quotients prove principal degree zero, giving Pic(P1)=Z by degree. Cleared actual powers become O(ma). Cohomology and Euler characteristics preserve degree under extension without a field-degree multiplier. Ampleness gives a>0.

C is algebraically closed: approximate monic polynomials by algebraic-coefficient polynomials with bounded roots; factorization supplies successive roots whose distances tend to zero, giving a limiting root by completeness. Induction gives factorization. Roots make the algebraic value group divisible. A sequence converging to a nonzero element eventually has its norm, so completion adds no nonzero values.

The Gauss orbit is finite because the splitting coordinates are defined over finite Galois E/K: Gal(overline K/E) fixes the coordinates and coefficient maxima. The action on C is the continuous isometric extension of this algebraic action. Coefficient automorphisms preserve disk radii. Algebraic automorphisms act through PGL2 via their action on H0(O(1)). Translation and scaling preserve logarithmic lengths. Inversion sends ζ(b,r) to ζ(b^{-1},r/|b|²) for r<|b|; for r≥|b|, ζ(b,r)=ζ(0,r) and its image is ζ(0,r^{-1}). Subdivision at meeting disks checks arbitrary finite arcs and the equality boundary. Type II is preserved.

The finite hull has type-II meeting vertices, radius max(r,s,|b−c|), and finite lengths in the value group. For diameter endpoints A,B of distance D, an attachment at coordinate t and height h satisfies h≤min(t,D−t). Their midpoint has radius D/2. Conversely its two endpoint distances force every minimum-radius center to have t=D/2 and h=0. The center is unique and fixed by every isometry. Singleton and two-point orbits are included. Divisibility realizes the midpoint radius at an actual type-II point. No infinite compact-tree boundedness shortcut is used.

The independent basepoint-free sections cT0 and T1−bT0 genuinely realize Q's degree-one atom. Degree-ma monomials on the actual cleared bundle, with the complete FS expression divided by m, give measure aδ_y. The continuous metrics are finite energy. Their G-transforms have the same measure; Q's every-solution allpoint uniqueness and normalization against an invariant reference make the constants zero. D descends actual continuous psh, and O gives downstairs aδ_ξ.

Norming is verified separately. Every section Σb_jw^j of every cleared O(d) has reference norm bounded by max|b_j|, attained at the Gauss point; the second chart includes infinity. Thus every weighted FS maximum, with arbitrary real weights, has the same maximizing point. Surjectivity transfers suprema downstairs. Decreasing FS anchor values cannot tend to −∞ unless the whole endpoint does; otherwise their finite limit equals anchor value and supremum. This establishes the full N antecedent.

N gives the intrinsic equivalence for every positive Radon mass-a target. O gives MA(tu)=(1−t)aδ_ξ+tMA(u), and anchored energy gives B(tu)=t²B(u). The unit bound yields Aμ(u)≤U max(1,√B); maximizing −B+U+U√B gives U+U²/4. Coercivity is not treated as attainment.

D preserves lifted mass and J for all upstairs continuous tests. The polarized isomorphism transports FS systems, actual endpoints, reference, energy, dual, and curvature; approximation transports operator covariance. Q supplies an actual upstairs solution. Equivariance and every-solution uniqueness followed by finite supremum normalization establish invariance. D first descends actual singular psh, then extended energy equality establishes downstairs E1 membership. Only afterward does O push the equation down.

For arbitrary two downstairs solutions, their upstairs measures are invariant and push to the same target. D identifies both with its unique invariant lift. Q identifies the metrics at every point modulo one finite constant; surjectivity transfers equality without subtracting pole values. No singular averaging is used. T handles trivial K; agreement with O follows continuously and along the same decreasing nets.

Concavity and O's exact segment derivative give the supporting-plane inequality and actual maximization. Weighted decreasing continuity against the fixed output identifies the continuous dual with the E1 maximum. Anchoring gives ∫u dμ=2E(u) and J=−E(u). Reference cocycles have the stated signs and finite corrections.

The Hahn arithmetic and completeness check. Well-ordered rational supports have well-ordered sum supports and finite convolution representations by nondecreasing-subsequence extraction. A positive minimum bounds summand counts below fixed exponent bounds, validating geometric-series inversion. Leading coefficients define the ordering; exponent-zero reduction gives residue R, and monomials give value group Q. For the chosen Cauchy subsequence, only finitely many difference supports contribute below each bound. Their locally finite union is well ordered and defines the limit. The field is complete, nontrivially and nondiscretely valued, with both characteristics zero.

The conic is smooth and geometrically integral, and ordering excludes K-points. Its parametrization satisfies the equation. The inverse pairs pull back to [2s²:2sr] and [2sr:2r²], recover [s:r], cover, and agree. The actual bundle pulls back to O(2), giving raw degree two; Čech cohomology and base change give genus zero. Conjugation acts by z↦−1/conjugate(z). With |2|=|i|=1, recovering 2s² and 2r² proves reference equality everywhere. The radius-e^{±1} disks form exactly a two-point orbit distinct from the fixed Gauss orbit. D distinguishes their quotient atoms. The tensor sum is an actual continuous metric with genuine two-atom measure; normalized uniqueness makes it invariant. Self-kernels one and cross-kernel zero give E=−1, integral −2, and J=1. O and Q establish finite dual.

The irrational-cycle caution and subdivision identity are correct and establish only arithmetic. Shell-free finite checks confirmed conic identities, two-atom bookkeeping, subdivision, and a symmetric finite tree. They certify no analytic descent. The complete pertinent GJKM Section 3 and BE Theorem 7.8/Corollary 7.9 units were read; their general-curve dependencies remain diagnostic background, unused here.

Harmless clarifications are the explicit inversion boundary, subdivision at meeting disks before calling pieces nested, division of the entire monomial FS expression by m, and qualification of residual equation gaps by the nontrivially valued scope because T grants the trivial boundary. No substantial repair is required.

Every external premise below was primary-source checked and its application reconstructed. The task-only passage is unindexed and excluded from external premises. Historical build diagnostics and provenance remain unchanged, unauthenticated data. No essential premise remains unresolved. The unrestricted positive-genus and higher-dimensional residual equation axes, P16.3, P16.7, and general nonample, singular, proper nonprojective, and nonalgebraizable axes remain open.

premises: Let k be a field, X a quasi-compact separated k-scheme, and F a quasi-coherent sheaf. A finite affine open cover and its affine finite intersections compute H^i(X,F) by the Čech complex. For every field extension k'/k and every i≥0, H^i(X_{k'},F_{k'}) is naturally H^i(X,F)⊗_k k'.
For every proper geometrically integral variety X over a field k, H^0(X,O_X)=k.
On a smooth integral curve over a characteristic-zero field, the local ring at every closed point is a discrete valuation ring, and every closed point is an effective Cartier divisor.
If X is a normal curve over a field k and Y is a proper k-variety, every k-rational map X⇢Y extends uniquely to a k-morphism X→Y.

For every proper curve X over a field k, every invertible sheaf M on X, and every field extension k'/k, deg_{k'}(M_{k'})=deg_k(M). Clearing denominators gives the same equality for actual rational line bundles.

For a complete real-valued non-Archimedean field K, the completion C of an algebraic closure with the extended absolute value is algebraically closed; completion preserves its nonzero absolute values, and log|C×| is divisible.

For well-ordered subsets A,B of Q, A+B is well ordered and each rational number has finitely many representations as a+b with a∈A and b∈B. If A consists of positive rationals, its set of finite sums is well ordered and each rational number has finitely many representations by finite ordered sequences of elements of A.
